observations: A rounded rectangular outline, doubled in rust-orange and blue, frames the central face shape against a dark teal-grey background with loose black marks at the edges.
Two eye forms sit in the upper half, each ringed by short radiating spikes in light blue; amber-orange irises glow at their centers against white.
A lower rectangular block holds four white vertical bars, flanked by yellow lines that drop below the chin and trail off the bottom edge.
reading: The face is built from hard-edged rectangles rather than curves, giving it a locked, mechanical feel that sits uneasily with the warm amber glow at each eye. White arcs and yellow lines run loose behind the structure, as though something fluid is trapped inside a rigid frame. The spiked rings around the eyes read as alert or wary—an emotional charge the rigid geometry keeps at a distance.
contextAngle: Within the owned nifty-faces subset, this work sits between title neighbors #62 and #64. Where #62 uses layered warm tones to build a naturalistic face, #63 replaces that softness with hard outlines and a dark ground, and #64 swings to saturated lime—showing the tonal range the collector values.

connections.reason: Title neighbor #64 shares the rectangular face outline and white vertical tooth bars, but floods the ground with bright lime rather than dark teal, making the two a direct color-mood contrast on the same structural idea.
nnotb #27 uses spiked radiating lines around its eye sockets and a similarly dark ground, making the spiky eye treatment a point of formal comparison across two series in the owned collection.

lookingQuestion: The yellow lines descend from the chin and continue below the face structure—where do they lead, and how does that affect the sense of where the figure ends?
ambiguities: The lower yellow lines and rectangular block could read as a neck or chin extension, but their exact structural role is unclear from the image alone.
Title-derived and recorded-creation order align for this work, but gaps exist elsewhere in the owned subset, so adjacency does not confirm sequential making.
